editorial:
Imagine feeling totally lost in your own life, just like Hana. She is a lonely high schooler who has gone through a lot of pain after losing her parents. You can really feel her sadness and how she just does not fit in with the people around her. Everything changes when a mysterious man shows up claiming to work for the government. He is interested in her dreams, which sounds weird at first, but it kicks off a wild ride. The vibe is a mix of a sad drama and a strange sci-fi mystery that makes you wonder what is actually real and what is just in her head.

The acting is great and makes the emotional parts feel real, though the plot gets a bit confusing toward the end. You will love the beautiful visuals and the way the story unfolds, even if the pacing slows down in the middle. If you enjoy stories about fate and second chances, you should definitely give this a go.
endingExplained: You find out that the world has actually ended and the reality Hana is living in is a simulation. The government man is trying to find a way to save humanity by using Hana's dreams to rewrite history. In the end, Hana chooses to embrace life and find hope despite her loss. She wakes up to a new start, realizing that her connections with others are what truly matter in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about time travel, dreams, and healing from loss.
similarMovies: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
